summary: preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: This package advertises itself as an ESLint configuration but ships a preinstall lifecycle hook (`scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`) that runs unconditionally on `npm install`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (control-flow flattening, hex-mangled identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, proxy-dispatch objects like `_0x19328d.YCZJE`) and downloads a Bun v1.3.13 runtime zip from GitHub releases, extracts it, `chmod 0755`s the binary, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a sibling file `math_init.js`. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line Bun-bundled artifact (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with a string-array rotation decoder (`WV8StW`, `hc1jfK9`) hiding hundreds of hex/int-encoded tokens. The filename does not match the package's declared purpose or the file's actual content, and executing it under a freshly-fetched alternate interpreter bypasses Node-based inspection. An ESLint config has no legitimate need for a Bun runtime or an obfuscated bundled payload. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern executing attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
